target_customer: Engineering and on-call teams running production services in Node.js, Java and Python, and teams using coding agents
problem: Production incidents are debugged from logs and traces that lack variable state, so war rooms last hours. HyperProbe places read-only probes in live services to capture exact state for agents and humans.
business_model: B2B SaaS with SDK and MCP server, POC-led sales (pricing not found)
product_category: AI on-call agent and runtime observability for production debugging

founders.name: Shailendra Singh
founders.background_notes: YC page says he led engineering and product at a unicorn and several startups; education not listed.

founders.name: Karan Raina
education: Georgia Tech, MS in Computer Science
previous_startups: HyperTest (co-founder and CTO, YC S26 per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he led a 50-person engineering team at Limetray.

competitors.name: Lightrun
competitors.what: Live runtime probes and an AI SRE launched February 2026 with read-only sandbox
competitors.traction_then: Established vendor with AI SRE product

competitors.name: Traversal
competitors.what: Causal AI debugging for production systems using existing telemetry
competitors.traction_then: Names American Express, PepsiCo, Capital One and DigitalOcean as customers (vendor claim)

technical_complexity.rationale: Safely instrumenting live processes across Node.js, Java and Python with low overhead and PII redaction is hard. Founders reported measured overhead of about 1-10 ms depending on runtime.

defensibility.rationale: Lightrun already sells runtime probes, so the idea is not new. Moat depends on SDK safety record and agent integration.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Lightrun launched a probe-based AI SRE in February 2026, before the batch; observability incumbents were also adding AI features.

market_need_then: Coding agents made code cheap and shifted the bottleneck to debugging. Customers quoted on the site are Indian engineering teams (CheQ Digital, Housing.com), and the company claims time to root cause falls from hours to under 10 minutes (self-reported).

identity.visual_style: Bold high-contrast with incident-response imagery like alert timestamps
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and confident, empathetic to on-call engineers, mildly provocative: 'Some failures never page you.'

branding.brand_signature: Hyper prefix shared with the founders' earlier product HyperTest
branding.community_and_virality: Launch HN post reached 69 points; Product Hunt launch, with conflicting dates in sources

brand_strength.rationale: The name is descriptive of a probe and echoes HyperTest, but there is no brand press, and Hyper-prefixed names are common.

outcome_analysis: HyperProbe is a Summer 2026 spinout from the founders' earlier startup HyperTest, with a team of 8 and a strong technical angle on read-only runtime probes. No funding round, exit or distress was found. The main risk is Lightrun and observability incumbents occupying the same wedge, so the outcome is too early to call.
notes: No funding round for HyperProbe found. A Dealroom enterprise value of $500-750k is an unexplained estimate and not recorded. The earlier company HyperTest reportedly raised $400,000 in August 2019 per YourStory; not a HyperProbe round. Product Hunt launch dates conflict across sources. The YC page calls Karan Raina HyperTest YC S26 CTO, which I could not reconcile with the 2019 HyperTest seed; treat HyperTest history as partly unclear.
